name: Foundations — Follow-up Visit Basics
_note: For pre-clinical (MS1-2) IMGs with no prior patient experience, practising the established-patient review loop for the first time. Scores LANGUAGE and COMMUNICATION, never advanced clinical reasoning — metric keys are kept identical to the standard follow_up rubric so scores/DB columns keep working, only the labels/anchors are re-pitched for a beginner reading a simple one-problem chart. The live checklist always comes from the case's own `learning_objectives` (see FollowUpEvaluation.canonicalChecklist), so the `checklist` below is a fallback only.

anchors.90-100: Clear, well-formed questions and sentences throughout
anchors.70-80: Occasional minor errors; meaning always clear
anchors.50-60: Some errors in tense/articles/word order, but understandable
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors; the patient must work to understand
anchors.10-20: Errors make most sentences hard to follow

anchors.90-100: Correct, natural everyday words for symptoms, side effects and taking medicine
anchors.50-60: Uses vague words where a simple clinical term would help, or small misuses
anchors.30-40: Often reaches for the wrong word or cannot find the term

anchors.90-100: Clearly links today's visit to what happened before and reaches a simple, sensible next step
anchors.70-80: Reviews the prior plan and interval change with only minor gaps
anchors.50-60: Asks some follow-up questions but the link to the previous visit is unclear or incomplete
anchors.30-40: Visit does not meaningfully check back on the prior plan
anchors.10-20: No coherent follow-up reasoning is demonstrated

anchors.90-100: Smooth, steady pace; clearly understandable pronunciation
anchors.70-80: Occasional hesitation; pronunciation rarely impedes understanding
anchors.50-60: Noticeable pauses or pronunciation that needs listener effort
anchors.10-20: Halting delivery or pronunciation that blocks understanding

anchors.90-100: Warm and nonjudgmental throughout, especially when asking about missed doses or difficulty following the plan
anchors.70-80: Good empathy; asks about adherence and side effects without blame
anchors.50-60: Adequate but mechanical; tone occasionally sounds like an interrogation
anchors.30-40: Little warmth; questions about adherence sound judgmental
anchors.10-20: Dismissive or unprofessional; patient is made to feel blamed

checklist.item: greeted the patient and confirmed the reason for today's follow-up
asked an open-ended question about how things have been since the last visit
asked whether the treatment or plan is working
asked about taking the medicine or plan as directed, using neutral, nonjudgmental language
asked about side effects or new symptoms
invited the patient's questions or concerns
agreed on a clear, simple next step (what happens now, or when to return)

empathy_markers: used neutral, nonjudgmental language when asking about missed doses or difficulty following the plan
acknowledged the effort or difficulty of ongoing treatment
invited the patient's questions and preferences
checked the patient's understanding of the updated plan
